Using the latest version of Claude Code, macOS and Linux users can now send messages between different work sessions, share findings, ask questions, and coordinate tasks. Details as follows.

Claude Code adds cross-session messaging feature

Anthropic announced a new feature yesterday, which should be very useful for users who frequently run multiple Claude Code sessions simultaneously.

Starting from Claude Code version 2.1.224, different sessions can send messages to each other, sharing updates and other relevant information. This feature is particularly useful for multiple sessions handling different parts of the same project simultaneously.

Below is the documentation released by Anthropic for this new feature:

Anthropic stated that the best use cases for this new feature include: handing over work, coordinating parallel worktrees, checking the status of long-running programs, and replying to messages across machines.

The company further pointed out that users do not need to write the message content themselves. Users only need to write down what they want to convey in the prompt, and Claude will draft the actual message on their behalf.

It is worth noting that the cross-session messaging feature does not apply to permission approval requests or changing settings. Commands like /compact will be sent as plain text rather than being executed as actual commands; moreover, if handling the message requires permission, the receiving party will still request approval from the user.
